final_candidates.decision_summary: Introduces an N-V-S sequon in C2, likely shielding CD4 binding-site accessibility while remaining outside conserved core contacts.
Creates an N-Y-S sequon in the exposed V2 loop, potentially reducing antibody recognition without disrupting trimer integrity.
Adds an N-S-T sequon in C2, providing an additional glycan shield with likely minimal structural perturbation.

stop_reason.detail: Further self-iteration is unlikely to improve confidence without experimental evidence; final candidates are based on structural rationale and sequence-validated glycosylation sites.

history.rationale: Introduces an N-linked glycosylation sequon (N-Y-S) in the V2 loop, potentially shielding a key neutralization epitope without disrupting conserved cysteines.
V2-loop glycan is well placed to shield neutralization epitopes and is flexible; raise confidence above redundant C2 candidates.
Adds a glycan (N-I-T) just after V2, likely affecting antibody access to the CD4 binding site while maintaining structural integrity.
Retain but at lower confidence; may create a glycan near V2 but potential steric clash with conserved core cannot be ruled out.
Creates a sequon (N-V-S) in C2, a conserved region near the V2 loop, potentially increasing glycan shielding without affecting core contacts.
Retain as top candidate; the C2-loop glycan likely reduces CD4 binding site accessibility without disrupting conserved contacts.
Forms an N-V-S motif in C2, adding a bulky glycan that may reduce antibody binding while remaining distal to functional hot spots.
Retain with slightly reduced confidence; adjacent to V241N and may have overlapping effect.
Generates an N-S-T sequon in C2, similar to S240N but at an adjacent residue, offering an alternative site for glycan shielding.
Retain at moderate confidence; C2 glycan may have redundant effect with S240N but adds alternative surface shielding.
